criteria.text: Recognizes that the three perturbations differ in modality: the genetic deletion and the PROTAC both remove PRMT7 protein (the PROTAC by VHL-directed proteasomal degradation, with Prmt7 mRNA unchanged), while the catalytic inhibitor leaves PRMT7 protein in place and blocks only its methyltransferase activity.

grounding.quote: These results strongly suggest that MS54 induced PRMT7 degradation via the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS).

criteria.text: Uses that modality difference to group the PROTAC degrader with the genetic deletion rather than with the catalytic inhibitor - despite the degrader being built from the same PRMT7-binding chemotype as the inhibitor - citing that in T cells the degrader lowers PRMT7 protein and raises nuclear p65 as the deletion does.

grounding.quote: Similarly, treatment with MS54 resulted in Prmt7 degradation and increased p65 nuclear localization in T cells relative to DMSO-treated controls (Figure 5J).

criteria.text: Recognizes that an enzymatically inactive PRMT7 mutant binds p65 and represses p65-driven NF-kB reporter activity as strongly as wild-type PRMT7.

grounding.quote: Increasing amounts of expression vectors encoding GFP-PRMT7WT or GFP-PRMT7DEAD into sgCTL and sgPRMT7 B16.F10 melanoma cells repressed the p65-mediated luciferase activity, in a dose-dependent manner, suggesting that Prmt7 represses NF-κB activity in a methyltransferase-independent manner (Figure 3I).

criteria.text: Uses the equal repression by the inactive mutant to conclude that blocking PRMT7's methyltransferase activity does not relieve its restraint on p65, so the catalytic inhibitor cannot reproduce the CD8+ expansion that follows removal of the protein.

grounding.quote: Both GFP-PRMT7WT and GFP-PRMT7 DEAD co-immunoprecipitated equally with FLAG-p65 when adjusted to input (Figure 3F).

criteria.text: Recognizes that PRMT7-deficient T cells show higher nuclear p65, higher NF-kB target-gene expression including the survival genes Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL, and down-regulated apoptosis programmes.

grounding.quote: Moreover, we validated the increased expression of several NF-κB target genes including iNos, ICAM, Bcl-2, Bcl-xL, and CD25 in CD8+ T cells using RT-qPCR (Figure 3D).

criteria.text: Uses that NF-kB profile, with the BAY 11-7082 dependence of the CD8+ difference, to conclude that removing PRMT7 protein raises rather than lowers the CD8+ fraction, so neither protein-removal arm can be the arm in which CD8+ cells fell to about 11%.

grounding.quote: Flow cytometry analysis revealed that the increased CD8+ T cell population in Prmt7 cKO mice was abolished with BAY 11-7082 (Figures 4A, 4B).

criteria.text: Rules out the alternative that the catalytic inhibitor simply failed to reach PRMT7, citing that pre-treatment with it abolishes PROTAC-mediated PRMT7 degradation and so demonstrates target engagement inside cells.

grounding.quote: Pre-treatment with either SGC3027 (a prodrug of SGC8158) or VHL101 completely abolished MS54-induced Prmt7 degradation (Figure 5E).
